Despite stepping into 2022 with new hopes after the pandemic, 
the world continued to face instability with the conflict in 
Ukraine and climate change. The world economy witnessed 
increased inflation, rising prices of raw materials, risks to energy 
security, global food security, and the tendency for tightened 
monetary policies from major central banks.
 
Choosing to not only recover, but also to 
prepare the momentum to contribute to the 
continued development and stabilization of 
the country’s economy and society, “Digital 
transformation – Comprehensive financial 
connection” is the key message that Military 
Commercial Joint Stock Bank (MB) focuses on 
in the year 2022. MB believes that together, 
focusing on digital acceleration – customer 
attraction – group synergy – sustainable 
reliability 
is 
the 
destination 
bringing 
prosperity to the company, the country, and 
the people in this challenging context.
Digital transformation 
– Comprehensive
financial connection
is the inevitable trend from global banking brands after the 
COVID-19 pandemic. With the motto of the customer as the 
focus, MB strongly promotes the utilization of technology to 
enhance its products and services, aiming to bring a seamless 
multi-channel banking experience to the customers, from mobile 
platforms and 24/7 self-service channels such as MB Smartbank, 
creating cashless interactions in everyday activities for customers, 
individual and businesses, anytime, anywhere. MB are pioneers 
in combining digitalization with humanitarian activities, with the 
Charity App – the first technology platform in Vietnam to openly 
and transparently support charity activities, directly connecting 
those wishing to donate to potential benefactors, spreading good 
things in society.
It can be said, MB is gradually realizing its goal of becoming a 
technological company, a fully digitally transformed company. 
Building convenience, user-friendly experiences, focusing on 
the user’s benefit, leading to increased customer attraction and 
satisfaction.
A solid foundation shall be formed by the connection of solid 
links. MB Group is the overall harmonious link combining its 6 
subsidiary companies, covering all areas of life and finance. 
MB lays the strong foundation that has been accumulated 
throughout a long period of time, providing a stepping stone for 
its subsidiary companies to launch, develop, and rise. In return, 
MB also receives positive business values and the potential to 
scale up the business in a speedy but sustainable way. MB is 
proud to possess a financial ecosystem complete in every area, 
boosting its competitive edge, bringing added values to the 
community, our partners, customers, employees, and relevant 
stakeholders.
The entirety of this process, Digital transformation – focusing 
on the customer will be the guiding motto for the group’s 
business activities. The year 2022 is the premise of the group’s 
strategic period 2022 – 2026 set out in general, and the year 
2023 in particular. In 2023, MB aims to increase productivity, 
reaching for the top position in the industry through the process 
of accelerating digitalization, automating operations and 
optimizing processes, continuously researching and presenting 
credit policies, and action programs responding to social and 
environmental risks. Unwavering, MB group will become a multi- 
functional financial group with a complete ecosystem based on 
the core motto “Comprehensive digital transformation” to better 
meet the needs of customers. Developing sustainably together 
will help MB develop a strong shield, ready to face difficulties and 
challenges from an unpredictable global society and community.

Dear Shareholders, Investors, and Partners,
In 2022, MB achieved various pride-worthy milestones, despite the 
context of global economic instability and difficulties. Following 
that, MB continues to maintain the leading position in digital 
transformation in the Finance – Banking industry, Top 30 largest 
enterprises in Vietnam, Top 4 commercial banks in profit and scale.
Although the global business environment has recovered after the 
Covid-19 pandemic, the world’s economy continues to be affected 
– recession being caused by confrontation events between the 
West and Russia, the war between Russia-Ukraine, China’s self- 
quarantine, etc. Vietnam’s economy was affected by the decrease 
in world demand, sharp increase in inflation and interest rates; 
accompanied by difficulties in the real estate industry, the corporate 
bond market, the trend of rising interest rates in the fourth quarter. 
With the Government’s flexible policies, these difficulties have been 
controlled accordingly, creating various opportunities to promote 
business efficiency for enterprises. In 2022, Vietnam’s GDP growth 
rate reached 8.02%, the highest in recent years. CPI has been 
controlled at 3.15% – lower than the target set by the State, and total 
investment of the entire society reached VND 3,219.8 thousand billion, 
an 11% increase compared to 2021.
2022 saw strong growth in digital transformation in the Banking - 
Finance sector with the following numbers: cashless transactions 
increased by 85.6% in quantity and 31.39% in value, advanced 
transactions methods such as QR Code doubled in both quantity 
and value compared to 2021 (according to studies by the State 
Bank); Vietnam places second in the world in terms of percentage 
smartphone users to make payment transactions (according to 
a report by Statista – Germany); advanced 4.0 technologies are 
strongly and widely applied by credit organizations in business 
activities.
As one of the Banking and Finance institutions to embrace the 
digitalization trend, 2022 is the first year for the group’s new strategic 
development period 2022-2026, with the goal “Top 3 enterprises in 
in terms of efficiency, aiming for the Top in Asia”, the vision “To 
become a digital enterprise, a Leading Financial Group”, and 
the motto “Digital Acceleration – Customer Attraction – Group 
Synergy – Sustainable Reliability”.
Message from 
The Chairman
The whole system of MB Group with great determination has 
successfully and excellently completed the 2022 plans assigned by 
the General Shareholder’s Meeting (GSM), specifically:
Indicators on scale of total assets, charter capital, profit before tax 
increased by 20 – 38% compared with 2021, exceeding objectives 
for 2022, of which: the group’s total assets reached VND 728.5 trillion, 
charter capital reached VND 45.3 trillion, profit before tax reached 
VND 22.7 trillion (Bank reached VND 20.3 trillion). Risk was carefully 
controlled with the NPL ratio kept at 1.09% (bank only at 0.83%, 
NPL coverage ratio was 295%), the safety limits comply with the 
regulations of the State Bank, efficiency targets were continuously 
reinforced: ROE at 25.55% (bank only at ~25.11%), CIR28.52% 
(nearly 1% decrease compared with 2021).
In addition to successfully completing the business plan, the Board of 
Directors (BOD) has effectively implemented the resolutions assigned 
by the 2022 GSM, completed dividend payment using shares at the 
rate of 20%, raising the charter capital of MB to VND 45,340 billion; 
establishing a bank with 100% MB capital in Cambodia, in operation 
since January 2, 2023; with the orientation focused towards digital 
and retail business, according to Group Strategy.
Digital transformation continues to achieve new achievements 
in 2022, affirming the pioneer position on the market with 02 key 
digital products: App MBBank (for individual customers) and BIZ 
MBBank (for business customers), which are continuously being 
improved, upgraded, receiving the Sao Khue prize in IT (Information 
and Technology) for 4 consecutive years (2019 – 2022), helping MB 
to develop 7 million new customers in 2022, reaching a cumulative 
number of 20 million customers, the rate for digital conversion in 
business customers at 75%, and 95% of all transactions being 
conducted digitally – Top within Vietnam’s banking industry. Revenue 
from digital channels in 2022 increased twofold compared to 2021, 
contributing to 17% of the Bank’s revenue.
MB’s network is modernized with 309 transaction points licensed to 
operate in Vietnam and overseas, 52 MB Smartbanks – providing 
an advanced experience and service, attracting customers, 
bringing MB to the position of Top 1 in the market with 1.8 billion 
transactions (increased twofold compared with 2021), 60 million 
transactions via Auto Bank (MB Smartbank and ATM), an 40% 
increase compared with 2021.
For governance activities, MB applies the most advanced technologies 
according to consultations by our partners, IBM, McKinsey, Gartner. 
These include AI/machine learning, BigData, Robotic, helping MB 
increase the rate of automation for more internal processes, gradually 
approaching advanced practices globally.
MB’s subsdiaries achieved impressive growth with total revenue 
reaching VND 23.7 trillion (up 30% compared to 2021), profit before 
tax reaching VND 2.7 trillion (up 18% compared to 2021), taking up 12% 
of the Group’s profit before tax. MB’s subsidiaries focus on investing 
in, improving IT infrastructure and technology, digital transformation, 
completing the group’s digital ecosystem, strengthening its position 
in the market. Additionally, MCredit achieved Top 3 in outstanding 
loans, ranking among the top in efficiency; MBAL achieved top 8 
in annual premium equivalent, Top 6 in Bancassurance contributes 
to helping MB maintain the Top 1 position in Bancassurance; MIC 
reached top 5 in market share, etc.
MB units consistently adheres to and respect the Law, actively 
participates in gratitude movements, social security work. MB 
effetively deployed the digital Charity platform, which is supported 
and trusted by the community, local authorities, and social 
organizations.
In 2023, with the proclamation “Digital transformation – 
Comprehensive financial connection”, MB’s vision is to continue to 
complete, strongly implement and optimize the Strategic Initiatives 
under the Group’s strategic period 2022 – 2026, promoting “Group 
Synergy”, coupled with strict risk management, ensuring liquidity, 
improving efficiency in every customer segment, strengthening 
MB’s presence in various locations, prioritizing key economic 
sectors and fields, green economic development; continue to 
improve the capacity of digital and technology transformation on 
the Group’s scale, ensuring security and confidentiality of data for 
customers and for MB.
Although the road ahead is still full of difficulties with pressing issues 
of climate change, geopolitical risks, and other emerging transition 
risks, MB is determined to develop a solid technology foundation 
that is the backbone to bring many values and benefits to MB, 
customers, communities, and other stakeholders, research solutions 
to contribute to the roadmap to realize the commitment to achieve 
net zero emissions by 2050 of the country.
With the challenging goal for MB to become a “Multifunctional 
financial group, reaching out to the region and the world” the 
BOD, Board of Management (BOM), and the Supervisory Board 
(SB) of MB are determined to make efforts to deploy flexible and 
creative management solutions created for MB’s management and 
administration for MB to grow sustainably along with enhancing 
business efficiency, quality of services; helping MB achieve more 
feats by balancing interests of stakeholders; affirming MB’s position 
as pioneers and leaders in digital transformation in the Finance – 
Banking industry in Vietnam. 
On behalf of the Board of Directors, I would like to extend my sincere 
gratitude to our Shareholders, Investors, Partners, customers and especially 
the entire MB staff and employees for accompanying us throughout 
this past year. We hope to continue to receive your cooperation, mutual 
agreement, and trust in the coming years.
Colonel General Le Huu Duc
Chairman of the Board of Directors

Message from the
Vice Chairman
Cum Chief Executive Officer
During 2022, continuing to be resolute, 
sticking to the goal of reaching “Top 3 
most efficient companies, aiming for the 
Top list in Asia”, MB focuses on organizing 
safe and sustainable business activities in 
all aspects of the Bank’s and the Group’s 
activities. From implementing safe and 
effective business, focusing on the life and 
health of employees, ensuring the interests 
of shareholders, investors and adding new 
value for customers, to responsibility to the 
community and society
Following the initiatives in the strategic period 2022 – 2026 closely, 
with the motto “Digital acceleration – Customer Attraction 
– Group Synergy – Sustainable Reliability” and the vision “To 
become a digital enterprise, a Leading Financial Group”, MB is 
one of the banks that have excelled in reaching the finish line in 2022 
with the Top 5 position in terms of profit, Top in return on capital and 
in the Top in safety indicators, credit quality.
MB had an impressive journey with many breakthrough 
achievements in digital transformation: MB recorded nearly 7 million 
new customers. The number of transactions on digital channels of 
MB ranks first in the market with 95% of transactions done on digital 
channels. Taking the “customer-centric” philosophy, MB continues to 
strongly digitalize, constantly “attracting customers” by launching 
new modern, market-leading products and services with high 
technology content, thereby providing excellent experiences, and 
adding new value to customers.
In addition to new consumer trends such as Mobile Money, Artificial 
Intelligence (AI), etc. gradually appearing after the Covid-19 
pandemic with a high potential for development, the macro context 
remains uncertain in the coming period with emerging risks such 
as transition risks from politics and climate change. Accordingly, 
MB continues to accelerate comprehensive digital transformation, 
innovate and develop outstanding products in the market to create 
excellent experiences for customers through building a digital 
ecosystem that serves and responds to every customer needs on 
2 digital platforms, App MBBank and BIZ MBBank, designing a 
seamless customer journey from offline to online, helping customers 
to have a “comprehensive financial connection”, contributing to 
bringing positive impacts to customers, the environment, society, 
and the economy.
At MB, we determine that applying technology in banking 
activities does not only help MB achieve its business goals but also 
reduces emissions, contributing towards sustainable development. 
Specifically, using MB’s digital platforms such as the MBbank APP, 
BIZ MBBank or the self-service model of MB Smartbank allows 
customers to actively transact 24/7, anytime, anywhere, while helping 
to reduce emissions from paperwork, as well as reducing time and 
emissions from customers going to the branch.
With 6 core values “Solidarity – Discipline – Dedication – Execution 
– Reliability – Efficiency”, MB orients management activities to 
ensure discipline, strictly abides by the provisions of the Law, Charter 
and standards selected by MB, ensuring a close relationship with 
stakeholders, in order to bring high efficiency to the whole Group. 
In addition, MB also constantly strives to provide employees with a 
safe, cohesive and motivating working environment with appropriate 
policies and benefits.
Regarding the environment and society, MB focuses on social 
security activities, implementing responsibility to the community 
through digital transformation in humanitarian activities. During the 
past year, MB has presided over the construction and development 
of the Charity Application, aiming for transparency and convenience 
for charity participants. With a strong investment in both platform 
and communication, MB’s Charity App currently owns more than 
1 million users and will be the backbone for other humanitarian 
platforms.
Of note, in 2022, the campaign “Covering Vietnam Green with MB” 
was officially launched by MB in partnership with Song Foundation 
to raise funds for the afforestation of 14 hectares of forest in Ninh 
Thuan, along with the goal of spreading media awareness on 
climate change in Vietnam. With the convenience and the ability to 
spread, the campaign has so far attracted nearly 100,000 supporters 
with more than 1 million supports, becoming one of the largest 
crowdfunding community campaigns in Vietnam.
In addition, financial inclusion is another area that MB is paying 
close attention to with regard to digitalization, aiming to spread the 
coverage of our financial services by serving all customer segments, 
especially the Mass customer segment, including customers who in 
the past had difficulties approaching banking and financial services, 
individuals with low income or living in rural areas, helping reduce 
social inequality and stabilizing finances.
We sincerely thank and send our deep gratitude to Shareholders, 
investors, customers, and partners who have continued to trust and 
accompany MB. 2023 is the second year in the strategic period 
2022 – 2026. With ambitious goals and challenges ahead, MB 
hopes to continue to receive consent, support and companionship 
from Distinguished customers, Distinguished shareholders, Investors 
and the entire MB staff in this promising new journey, allowing MB 
gradually successfully complete the goals that have been set.
Mr. Luu Trung Thai
Vice Chairman of the Board of 
Directors cum Chief Executive Officer

Development 
Process
On November 4, 1994, Military Commercial 
Joint Stock Bank (MB) was established 
with a capital of nearly VND 20 billion, 25 
employees and a single transaction point 
at 28A Dien Bien Phu, Hanoi.
The first ten years since establishment 
(1994-2004) was a period for “paving 
the way” to shape the operating motto, 
determine the business strategy and 
define the brand. Persistent with its 
goals and long-term vision, MB steadily 
overcame the 1997 financial crisis and 
was the only profitable joint stock bank. 
In 2004, 10 years since establishment, MB’s 
total mobilized capital increased by 500 
times, with total assets valued at VND 7 
trillion, profits exceeded VND 500 billion 
and opened up a new headquarter at No. 
3 Lieu Giai Street, Ba Dinh District, Ha Noi.
From a bank with just 25 employees and VND 20 billion of charter 
capital, after 28 years, MB has transformed itself into a versatile 
financial group, constantly accelerating digital transformation, 
aiming to bring customers best experiences. As a member of the 
Vietnam Banks Association, MB has been actively contributing to 
the development of the banking and finance industry.

sustainable and safe development strategy

target of winning the position in the top 3 
list in 2013, two years ahead of schedule. In 
2014, MB was honored to receive the First-
Class Labour Medal for its achievements. 
Subsequently in 2015, MB was honored to 
be conferred the title “Hero of Labor”.

effectively 
in

Business Lines
Military Commercial Joint Stock Bank conducts activities of a 
commercial bank in accordance with regulations of the law and 
the State Bank of Vietnam, including the following activities:
FINANCIAL SERVICES ACTVITIES
Provide cash management service, consultancy of banking, finance, etc.; provide 
consultancy of corporate finance; provide fiduciary, trustee, agent in the field related 
to banking activities, insurance, asset management; trade valuable papers; invest in 
Government bonds future; offer other activities approved by the State Bank
WHOLESALE OF METALS AND METAL ORES
Trade gold bars
ACTIVITIES OF INSURANCE  
AGENTS AND BROKERS
Details according to license for establishment and operations of commercial joint stock banks no. 
100/ GP-NHNN dated October 16, 2018
OTHER CURRENCY INTERMEDIATION
Accept deposits, grant credit, open checking accounts, provide domestic payment 
services, organize internal payment, participate in national inter-bank payment system; 
participate in the bidding for purchase and sale of treasury bills, etc.; implement purchase 
and sale of government bonds, corporate bonds, currency brokerage services, issuance 
of deposit certificates, promissory notes, bills, bonds, etc., borrow from the State Bank; 
borrow, lend, receive and deposit funds from and to credit institutions and branches of 
foreign banks; contribute capital and purchase shares; trade, supply foreign currency 
services in domestic and international markets; trade and supply interest derivative 
products; securities custody; provide electronic wallet; provide commodity derivative 
products; purchase debts; and implement other activities approved by the State Bank

transaction offices in Vietnam, 3 transaction offices overseas)

In 2022 MB has started deploying its 11 strategic initiatives and its 
relevant projects. Aside from that, MB focuses on carrying out its 
core objectives, with no new projects.
1. Attracting customers according to segments on digital channels
Deploying business projects such as: Customer Onboarding, 
Retention, Upsale, Customer Service, Digital Lending, Trade 
Finance, MB Smartbank... allowing MB to attract over 7 million 
new accounts on the App MBBank and over 65.5 thousands new 
accounts on BIZ MBBank, increasing the ratio of customers on 
digital channels to 82%
2.  The platform App MBBank, BIZ MBBank serving all transaction 
needs of individual and corporate customers
With two central platforms, App MBBank for individual customers 
and BIZ MBBank for corporate customers, MB builds optimized 
experiences for each customer segment, increasing market 
competitiveness. In which, the App MBBank built a unique digital 
bank with financial and investment products personalized according 
to customer segments, Mass and Priority. The platform BIZ MBBank 
connects to the customer’s ERP, providing a complete suite of 
financial solutions. In 2022, the ratio of transactions conversion to 
digital channels reached 94.4%; revenue from digital channels 
increased 2.2 times compared with 2021.
MB’s digital ecosystem connects with over 200 businesses, integrating 
with solutions outside of banking through solutions such as Beyond 
Banking, Banking as a service as used by the platform Landstock, 
satisfying real estate transaction and informational needs for the 
customer; the platform Maketplace satisfying customers’ everyday 
financial needs; MB presided over the development of the Charity 
platform, supporting convenience for those wishing to donate 
to charities, with over 1 million users, becoming the pillar for other 
humanitarian digital platforms.

Activities of the Internal Audit Department 
ORGANIZATIONAL 
STRUCTURE
The Internal Audit Department is a 
division-level department, convenes at the 
Headquarters, belonging to the SB and 
is under the SB’s direction. The Internal 
Audit Department  directly reports to the 
SB in accordance with the law and MB’s 
internal regulations. The Internal Audit 
Department is the third defense line in the 
3-defense line model, conducting auditing 
on the effectiveness of the first and second 
defense line; conducting auditing and 
consultations on supervisory activities of 
senior management with the BOD, CEO. 
The Internal Audit Department has the 
function of managing the Group’s internal 
auditing activities; orientating, training 
and assessing the maturity of the group’s 
internal auditing activities.
FUNCTIONS
Reviewing, assessing independently and
objectively with regards to the internal 
auditing 
system; 
independently 
assessing the suitability and adherence 
to regulations, internal procedures and 
policies; recommending solutions to 
enhance the effectiveness of procedures, 
regulations, ensuring safety in activities, 
effectiveness, and adherence to the law. 
OPERATING PRINCIPLES 
The Internal Audit Department conducts 
activities 
independently, 
objectively, 
and professionally, controlling conflicts 
of interest.
Internal auditors are not to have 
responsibilities 
from 
individuals, 
bodies subject to internal audits; are 
not to have any interference when

responsibilities. 
Results from internal auditing reports are 
to be carefully analyzed according to 
data and information collected. Internal 
auditors are to ensure honesty during 
reporting 
and 
assessing, 
satisfying 
indicators on level of expertise and 
ethics; following the law and internal

delegated.

auditing activities of divisions with high risks.

Military Commercial Joint Stock Bank (“the Bank”) is a joint stock commercial bank 
incorporated and registered in the Socialist Republic of Vietnam.

Governor of the State Bank of Vietnam (“the SBV”) dated 17 October 2018, replacing 
Operating License No. 0054/NH-GP dated 14 September 1994. The operating duration 
under the licence is 99 years since 14 September 1994. The Bank is operating under 
Business Registration No. 0100283873 granted by the Hanoi Department of Planning and 
Investment on 30 September 1994 and the 50th amended Business Registration on 20 
October 2022. 
The current principal activities of the Bank are to perform banking services including 
mobilizing and receiving short, medium and long-term deposits from organizations and 
individuals; making short, medium and long-term loans to organizations and individuals 
based on the nature and capability of the Bank’s capital; conducting foreign exchange 
transactions, international trade finance services, discounting of commercial papers, 
bonds and other valuable papers; providing settlement services and other banking 
services as approved by the SBV.

3.4 Basis of consolidation
	
The consolidated financial statements comprise the financial statements of the Bank 
and its subsidiaries for the year ended 31 December 2022.
Subsidiaries are fully consolidated from the acquisition date, on which the Bank obtains 
control and continue to be consolidated until the Bank terminates the control.
The financial statements of the Bank and its subsidiaries are prepared for the same

Debts are classified into following groups: Current, Special Mention, Sub-standard, 
Doubtful and Loss as specified in Circular 11. Debts which are classified as Sub-
standard, Doubtful and Loss are non-performing loans.
Debts are classified according to both quantitative and qualitative methods 
specified in Articles 10 and 11, Circular 11. Accordingly, if the results of the 
classification of a debt under Article 10 and Article 11 are different, then the debt

•	 If a customer has more than one debt with the Bank and any of the outstanding

Debt purchase
For the purchased debts, the Bank classifies the paid amount into a group with risk level not lower 
than previous debt group that was classified before purchase. Debt classification and provision

•	 The price of debt purchase under the contract is accounted on the statement of

of financial position;
•	 If the interest of the debt including the interest before the purchase is collected, the 
Bank will allocate the interest on the following principle: (i) write down the value of 
debt purchase by pre-purchase interest; (ii) recognize as interest income of the period 
after the Bank purchases the debt.
Debt sale
Revenue and expense from selling debts are recorded in accordance with Circular 09, the 
difference between the debt purchase, sale price and debt seller’s book value is handled 
as follows:
•	 For the debts being recorded on the statement of financial position:
	- If the debt sale price is higher than the book value of the debt, the difference shall be 
accounted as income of the Bank during the period.
	- If the debt sale price is lower than the value of the debt, the difference shall be 
offset with the compensation paid by an individual or an organization (in case 
such individual or organization is identified to have caused the damage and must 
pay compensation under regulations), the insurance sum paid by the insurer or the 
risk provision already set aside from expenses; the deficit shall be accounted as a 
business cost of the Bank.
For the debt accounted off the statement of financial position or debt left out of the 
statement of financial position, the debt sale proceeds shall be accounted as other 
income of the Bank.
4.7 Held-for-trading securities
Held-for-trading securities include debt securities, equity securities and other securities 
acquired and held for the purpose of trading. Held-for-trading securities are initially 
recognized at cost.
Listed debt held-for-trading securities are recognized at cost less provision for diminution 
in value of securities, which is based on the yield quoted on the Hanoi Stock Exchange at 
the statement of financial position date. 
Provision for credit losses of corporate bonds, which are not listed on the stock market 
or not registered on the unlisted public company market, is made in accordance with 
Circular 11 as described in Note 4.5.
Equity securities are recognized at cost. Periodically, provision for impairment of held-for-
trading securities is recorded when their book values are higher than their market values. 
In case the market values of the securities cannot be determined, no provision is made. 
Provision for impairment is recognized in the consolidated statement of profit or loss as 
“Net gain from held-for-trading securities”.
Gains or losses from sales of held-for-trading securities are recognized in the consolidated 
statement of profit or loss. Held-for-trading securities are derecognized when the 
rights to receive cash flows from these securities are terminated or when MB transfers 
substantially all the risks and rewards of ownership of these securities.

4.8 Investment securities
 
4.8.1 Available-for-sale securities
Available-for-sale securities include debt and equity securities listed on securities markets 
held by MB for the investment and available-for-sale purposes, not regularly traded but 
can be sold when there is a benefit. 
Available-for-sale equity securities are securities listed on securities markets. They are 
initially recognized at cost at the purchase date and continuously presented at cost in 
subsequent periods.
Available-for-sale debt securities are recognized at par value at the transaction date. 
Accrued interest (for debt securities with interest payment in arrears) and deferred interest 
(for debt securities with interest payment in advance) is recognized in a separate account. 
Discount/premium, which is the difference between the cost and the amount being the par 
value plus (+) accrued interest (if any) or minus (-) deferred interest (if any) is also recognized 
in a separate account. 
In subsequent periods, these securities are continuously recorded at par value, and the 
discount/premium (if any) is amortized to the consolidated statement of profit or loss on 
a straight-line basis over the remaining term of securities. The interest received in arrears 
is recorded as follows: Cumulative interest incurred before the purchase date is recorded 
as a decrease in the accrued interest; cumulative interest incurred after the purchase 
date is recognized as income based on the accumulated method. The interest received in 
advance is amortized into interest income on a straight-line basis over the term of securities 
investment.
Available-for-sale securities are subject to impairment review on a periodical basis. 
Provision for diminution in value of securities is made when the carrying value is higher 
than the market value. In case market prices of securities are not available or cannot be 
determined reliably, no provision is required. Provision is recognized in the “Net gain/(loss) 
from investment securities and long-term investments” of the consolidated statement of profit 
or loss.
Provision for credit losses of corporate bonds which are not listed on the stock market or 
not registered on the unlisted public company market is made in accordance with Circular 
11 as described in Note 4.5.
4.8.2 Held-to-maturity investment securities
Held-to-maturity securities are debt securities purchased by MB for the investment 
purpose of earning interest and MB has the capability and intention to hold these 
investments until maturity. Held-to-maturity securities have determined value and 
maturity dates. In case the securities are sold before the maturity date, the remaining 
portfolio of these securities will be reclassified to securities held-for-trading or available-
for-sale securities.
Held-to-maturity securities are recorded and measured similarly to debt securities 
available-for-sale and presented at Note 4.8.1.
4.9 Other long-term investments
Other long-term investments are investments in other entities in which MB holds less than 
or equal to 11% of voting rights and securities of these entities are not listed on the stock 
market. These investments are initially recorded at cost at the transaction date.
Provision for diminution in the value of investment is made when there is substantial 
evidence indicating a decline in the value of these investments at the statement of 
financial position date.
The provision is reversed if the recoverable amount of the investments increases after 
making provision, to the extent that the carrying value of these investments does not 
exceed the carrying value of the investments assuming that no allowance has been 
recorded.
 
Increase or decrease in provision for long-term investments is recognized in “Net gain/ 
(loss) from investment securities and long-term investments” on the consolidated statement 
of profit or loss.
4.10 Fixed assets
Fixed assets are stated at cost less accumulated depreciation or amortization. 
The cost of a fixed asset comprises its purchase price plus any directly attributable costs of 
bringing the asset to working condition for its intended use. 
Cost related to additions, improvements and renewals are capitalized while expenditures 
for maintenance and repairs are charged to the consolidated statement of profit or loss. 
When fixed assets are sold or liquidated, their cost and accumulated depreciation/
amortisation are deducted from the consolidated statement of financial position and any 
gains or losses resulting from their disposal (being the difference between net proceeds 
from the sale of assets and the remaining value of assets) are recorded to the consolidated 
statement of profit or loss.

4.15 Business combinations and goodwill
Business combinations are accounted for using the acquisition method. The cost of a 
business combination is measured as the fair value of assets given, equity instruments 
issued and liabilities incurred or assumed at the date of business combination plus any 
costs directly attributable to the business combination. Identifiable assets and liabilities 
and contingent liabilities assumed in a business combination of the acquiree are 
measured initially at fair value at the date of business combination. 
Goodwill acquired in a business combination is initially recognized at cost being the 
excess of the cost of the business combination over the acquirer’s interest in the net fair 
value of the acquiree’s identifiable assets, liabilities and contingent liabilities. If the cost 
of a business combination is less than the fair value of the net assets of the subsidiary 
acquired, the difference is recognized directly in the consolidated statement of profit 
or loss. After initial recognition, goodwill is recognized at cost less any accumulated 
amortization. Goodwill is amortized on a straight-line basis over a period of ten (10) years.
4.16 Re-purchase and reverse re-purchase contracts
Securities sold under agreements to repurchase at a specific date in the future (repos) 
are still recognized in the consolidated financial statements. The corresponding cash 
received from these agreements is recognized in the consolidated statement of financial 
position as a borrowing and the difference between the sale price and repurchase price is 
amortized in the consolidated statement of profit or loss over the term of the agreement 
using the straight-line method based on the interest rate stipulated in the contract.
	
Conversely, securities purchased under agreements to resell at a specific date in the 
future are not recognized in the consolidated financial statements. The corresponding 
cash paid under these agreements is recognized as a loan in the consolidated statement 
of financial position and the difference between the purchase price and resale price is 
amortized in the consolidated statement of profit or loss over the term of the agreement 
using the straight-line method based on the interest rate stipulated in the contract.
4.17 Leased assets
The determination of whether an arrangement is, or contains a lease is based on the 
substance of the arrangement at the inception date and requires an assessment of 
whether the fulfilment of the arrangement depends on the use of a specific asset and 
the arrangement conveys a right to use the asset. 
A lease is classified as a finance lease whenever the terms of the lease transfer 
substantially all the risks and rewards of ownership of the asset to the lessee. All other 
leases are classified as operating leases.
Where MB is the lessee
Rentals under operating leases are charged to the consolidated statement of profit or 
loss on a straight-line basis over the lease term.
Where MB is the lessor
Assets subject to operating leases are included as MB’s fixed assets in the consolidated 
statement of financial position. Initial direct costs incurred in negotiating an operating 
lease are recognised in the consolidated statement of profit or loss as incurred.  
Lease income is recognised in the consolidated statement of profit or loss on a straight-
line basis over the lease term.
4.18 Due to the Government and the State Bank of Vietnam
Due to the Government and the State Bank of Vietnam is recognized at cost
4.19 Deposits from other credit institutions and customers, other borrowed and 
entrusted funds and valuable papers issued
Deposits from other credit institutions, customer deposits, other borrowed and entrusted 
funds and valuable papers issued are disclosed at the principal amounts outstanding at 
the end of the financial year. At initial recognition, issuance costs are deducted from the 
cost of the valuable papers. These costs are allocated on a straight-line method during 
the lifetime of the valuable papers to “Interest and similar expenses”.
4.20 Foreign currency transactions 
According to accounting system of MB, all transactions are recorded in original currencies. 
Monetary assets and liabilities denominated in foreign currencies are translated into VND 
using exchange rates ruling at the consolidated statement of financial position date (Note 
54). Income and expenses arising in foreign currencies during the period are converted 
into VND at rates ruling at the transaction dates. Foreign exchange differences arising 
from the translation of monetary assets and liabilities are recognized in the consolidated 
statement of profit or loss.
4.21 Payables and accruals
Payables and accruals are recognized for amounts to be paid in the future for goods and 
services received, regardless of whether invoices have been received by the Bank from 
the supplier.

Covered warrants are securities with collateral issued by MB Securities Joint Stock 
Company, a member of MB, allowing the holder the right to purchase the underlying 
securities from the warrant issuer at a predetermined price, at or before a specified time, 
or receive the difference between the strike price and the underlying security’s price at 
the time of exercise.
Covered warrants are initially recognized at cost and continue to be recognized after 
initial recognition at fair value under the entry “Other payables and liabilities”.
Differences due to revaluation of covered warrants at fair value compared with the 
previous period are recognized in the consolidated statement of profit or loss under the 
item “Net gain/(loss) from held-for-trading securities”.
The costs of buying and issuing warrants are recognized in the consolidated statement 
of profit or loss as soon as they are incurred.
4.23 Technical reserves of insurance subsidiaries 
The technical reserves are calculated based on Circular No. 50/2017/TT-BTC dated 15 
May 2017 issued by the Ministry of Finance providing guidelines for financial regulations 
of insurers, reinsurers, insurance brokers and foreign non-life insurance branches (“Circular 
50”). Details of such reserving methodologies are as follows:
(i) Unearned premium reserves
Unearned premium reserve for insurance policies and reinsurance agreements with terms 
of less than or equal to 1 year is calculated as a percentage of total premium, as such:
•	 For line of insurance of cargo delivered by road, water, inland water, railway and 
airway: unearned premium reserve is made at 25% of the retained premium.
•	 For other non – life insurance lines with: unearned premium reserve is made at 50% 
of the retained premium.
•	 For life insurance: unearned premium reserve is calculated on the gross premium for all 
insurance policies with a term of one (1) year or less at the reporting date.
Unearned premium reserve for insurance policies and reinsurance agreements with terms 
of more than 1 year:
•	 For non-life insurance: unearned premium reserve is made by the formula as follows:
(ii) Mathematical reserve
Mathematical reserve for life insurance is the difference between the present value of total 
insurance payables in the future and the present value of the net insurance premiums 
with Zillmer adjustment for insurance premiums receivables in the future. Mathematical 
reserve is calculated for insurance policies that have valid period of more than one (1) 
year with specific actuarial formulae and factors for each type of products as registered 
and approved by the Ministry of Finance. The maximum valuation interest rate is linked 
to the average interest rate of government bonds as per formula specified in the Circular 
01/2019/TT-BTC.
(iii) Claims reserve
Claim reserve includes the reserve for outstanding claims and for claims incurred but not 
reported. 
•	 Outstanding claim reserve is established based on the estimated claim payments 
for each claim for which the insurer is liable, which is either notified to the insurer or 
requested for payment but is still unresolved at the end of the fiscal year; and
•	 Reserve for incurred but not reported claims for which the insurer is liable (IBNR) is 
established according to regulations in Circular 50.
Gross and assumed reinsurance claim reserve is presented as current liabilities; claim 
reserve of outward reinsurance is presented as “Other external receivables“.

(iv) Catastrophe reserve
Catastrophe reserve is made annually until it reaches 100% of the retained premiums of 
the accounting period and based on 1% of retained premiums according to Circular 50. 
On 28 December 2005, the Ministry of Finance issued Decision No. 100/2005/QD-BTC 
governing the publication of four new accounting standards, including Vietnamese 
Accounting Standard (“VAS”) 19 – Insurance Contract. Accordingly, from January 2006, 
the provision of catastrophe reserve is no longer required since it represents “possible 
claims under contracts that do not exist at the reporting date”. However, since the 
Ministry of Finance has not issued detailed guidance for the implementation of VAS 
19 and according to Decree No. 73/2016/ND-CP issued by the Government of Vietnam 
dated 1 July 2016 on details of the implementation of the Law on Insurance Business 
and amendments to certain articles of the Law on Insurance Business (“Decree 73”), MB 
continues to make catastrophe reserve on the consolidated financial statements for the 
fiscal year ended 31 December 2022.
(v) Equalization reserve  
Equalization reserve for health insurance is established at  one percent (1%) of its profit before 
tax, annually for reserve until this reserve reaches five percent (5%) collected premiums in the 
fiscal year of MB Ageas Life Insurance Company Limited.

4.25 Recognition of income and expenses
Income and expenses from banking operation
Interest income and expenses are recognized in the consolidated statement of profit 
or loss on an accrual basis. The recognition of accrued interest income of a loan is 
suspended when such debt is classified in groups 2 to 5 in compliance with Circular 11 or 
restructured under Circular 01. Suspended interest income is reversed and monitored off-
statement of financial position and recognized in the consolidated statement of profit or 
loss upon actual receipt.
Fees and commissions are recognized when the services are performed.
For other income, when the result of the contract is definitely determined, income is 
recognized based on the stage of completion of work or service. If the result of the 
contract is not determined, income is only recognized to the extent of recoverable 
amount of expenses incurred.
According to Circular No. 16/2018/TT-BTC dated 7 February 2018 by the Ministry of 
Finance guiding some articles on financial regime for credit institution, foreign bank 
branch, receivables from uncollectible accrued income at the due date are recorded as 
reduction in revenue if the income has been accrued in the same accounting period or 
recorded as expense if the income has been accrued in different accounting periods and 
monitored off-statement of financial position. Upon actual receipt of these receivables, 
MB would recognize to “Other income” on the consolidated statement of profit or loss.
Income from securities trading business
Income from securities trading is determined by the difference between the selling price 
and the weighted average cost of the securities.
Cash dividends are recognized in the consolidated statement of income when the right to 
receive cash dividends of MB is established. Dividends received in the form of common shares, 
bonus shares and stock options for current shareholders, shares distributed from undistributed 
profits are not recognized as an income of MB but only update the number of stock.
Income from insurance business
Gross written premiums are recognized in accordance with Circular 50/2017/TT-BTC.
Income from real estate business
	
Income is recognized to the extent that it is probable that the economic benefits will flow 
to MB. Income is measured at the fair value of the consideration received or receivable, 
excluding trade discount, rebate and sales returned. 
Income is recognised when MB has passed significant risks and rewards associated with 
the real estates to the buyers and income can be reliably measured.
Claim expenses for insurance activities
Claim expenses of gross premium is recognized on the basis of incurrence when MIC and 
MB Ageas accept claims.
Claim expenses for reinsurance premiums assumed is recognized upon incurrence in 
accordance with the statement of the reinsurer which was sent to MIC and MB Ageas 
and accepted by MIC and MB Ageas.
Claim receivables for reinsurance premiums ceded are recognized upon actual incurrence 
in accordance with the receivable amount corresponding to claim expense recognized 
during the period and the rate of reinsurance ceded.
Other expenses for insurance activities are recognized when incurred.   
Commission expenses for insurance business
Commission is calculated at certain percentage of direct premiums for specific line of 
insurance as stipulated in Circular 50. Commission expenses are allocated and recognized 
in the consolidated statement of profit or loss for direct premiums earned during the 
period. The commission which is not allocated would be recognized as prepaid expense 
and being allocated in the subsequent periods.
Loan origination costs from loan to customers in the finance company
Loan origination costs including commissions to agencies, third parties, and sale personnel 
are amortized into the consolidated statement of profit or loss using the straight-line 
method over the average duration of the loan product types ranging from 9 - 29 months.

4.26 Corporate income taxes
Current income tax
Current income tax assets and liabilities for the current and prior periods are measured 
at the amount expected to be recovered from (or paid to) the taxation authorities - 
using the tax rates and tax laws applied and enacted at the consolidated statement of 
financial position date.
Current income tax is charged or credited to the consolidated statement of profit or 
loss except when it relates to items recognized directly to equity, in this case the current 
income tax is also recognized in equity.
Current income tax assets and liabilities are offset when there is a legally enforceable 
right for MB to offset current tax assets against current tax liabilities and when MB 
intends to settle its current tax assets and liabilities on a net basis.
Deferred tax
Deferred tax is provided on temporary differences at the consolidated statement of 
financial position date between the tax base of assets and liabilities and their carrying 
amount for the financial reporting purposes. 
Deferred tax payables are recognized for temporary taxable differences.
Deferred tax assets are recognized for all deductible temporary differences, deductible 
amounts carried over subsequent periods of taxable losses and unused tax credits when 
it is probable that there will be sufficient taxable profit to use deductible temporary 
differences, taxable losses and these unused tax credits.The carrying amount of deferred 
tax assets is reviewed at each statement of financial position date and reduced to the 
extent that it is no longer probable that sufficient taxable profit will be available to allow 
all or part of the deferred tax asset to be utilized. Previously unrecognized deferred tax 
assets are re-assessed at each statement of financial position date and are recognized to 
the extent that it has become probable that future taxable profit will allow the deferred 
tax assets to be recovered.
Deferred tax assets and deferred tax liabilities are determined on the basic of expected 
tax rate applied when assets are recovered or liabilities are settled, on the basis of tax 
rate and tax laws which effective at the end of the period.
4.27 Classification for off-statement of financial position commitments
According to Circular 11, credit institutions should classify guarantees, payment acceptances 
and irrevocable loan commitments with specific effective date (generally called “off-
statement of financial position commitments”) in compliance with Article 10, Circular 11 for 
management and monitoring of credit quality. Accordingly, off-statement of financial 
position commitments are classified into groups which are Current, Special Mention, 
Substandard, Doubtful and Loss based on the overdue status and other qualitative factors.
4.28 Derivatives
	
MB enters in currency forward contracts and swap contracts to facilitate customers to transfer, 
modify or mitigate foreign exchange risk or other market risks, and also for the business 
purpose of MB.
Currency forward contracts
The currency forward contracts are commitments to settle in cash on a pre-determined future 
date based on the difference between pre-determined exchange rates, and the notional 
amount of the contracts. The currency forward contracts are recognized at nominal value 
at the transaction date and are revalued periodically. Gains or losses from revaluation are 
recognized in the consolidated statement of profit or loss.
Swap contracts
The swap contracts are commitments to settle in cash on a pre-determined future date based 
on the difference between pre-determined exchange rates and the notional principal amount 
of the contracts or commitments to settle interest based on a floating rate or a fixed rate 
calculated on the notional amount and in a given period. 
The currency swap contracts are revalued periodically. Gains or losses realized or unrealized 
are recognized in the consolidated statement of profit or loss. 
Differences in interest rate swaps are recognized in the consolidated statement of profit or loss 
on an accrual basis.
4.29 Earnings per share
MB presents basic earnings per share for ordinary shares. Basic earnings per share amounts 
are calculated by dividing net profit or loss after tax for the year attributable to ordinary 
shareholders of MB (after adjusting for the bonus and welfare fund) by the weighted average 
number of ordinary shares outstanding during the year.
If the shares issued during the year only change the number of shares without changing 
the total equity, MB will adjust the weighted average number of ordinary shares currently 
circulated to the previous period presented on the consolidated financial statements, resulting 
in a corresponding adjustment of the opening balance of the basic earnings per shares.

4.30       Employee benefits
4.30.1	
Post-employment benefits 
Post-employment benefits are paid to retired employees of MB in Vietnam by the Social 
Insurance Agency of the Ministry of Labour, Invalids and Social Affairs. MB is required to 
contribute to these post-employment benefits by paying social insurance and occupational 
accident and disease insurance at the rate of 17% and 0.5% respectively of the employee’s 
basic monthly salary. Moreover, MB has no further obligation.
4.30.2 Voluntary resignation benefits
According to Article 46 of the Vietnam Labour Law 45/2019/QH14 entered into force from 1 
January 2021, MB has the obligation to pay allowance arising from voluntary resignation of 
employees, equal to one-half month’s salary for each year of employment up to 31 December 
2008 plus salary allowances (if any) for employee who voluntarily resign and fully satisfy the 
requirements as prescribed by law. The average monthly salary used in this calculation is 
based on the average monthly salary of the latest six-month period up to the resignation 
date.
4.30.3 Unemployment benefits
According to Circular No. 28/2015/TT-BLDTBXH providing guidance for Decree No. 28/2015/
ND-CP dated 12 March 2015 on unemployment insurance, from 1 January 2009, MB is required 
to contribute to the unemployment insurance at the rate of 1% of salary and wage fund 
of unemployment insurance joiners and deduct 1% of monthly salary and wage of each 
employee to contribute to the Unemployment Insurance Fund.
4.31 Segment reporting
A segment is a separate unit of MB which participates in providing relevant products and 
services (segments categorized by business sectors) or providing products and services 
in a certain economic environment (segments categorized by geographical regions). Each 
segment bears unique risks and gains different benefits. The fundamental segment report 
form of MB is based on business sectors. 
4.32 Related parties
	
Parties are considered to be related parties of MB if a party has the ability to control the other 
party or exercise significant influence over the other party in making financial and operating 
decisions, or when MB and the other parties are under common control or under common 
significant influence.
4.33 Offsetting
Financial assets and financial liabilities are offset and the net amount is reported in the 
consolidated statement of financial position if, and only if, there is a currently enforceable 
legal right to offset financial assets against financial liabilities or vice-versa, and there is an 
intention to settle on a net basis, or to realize the assets and settle the liabilities simultaneously.

MB has the obligation to pay corporate income tax (“CIT”) at the rate of 20% of taxable 
profits in Vietnam according to Circular No. 78/2014/TT-BTC which became effective from 
2 August 2014, guiding the implementation of the Government’s Decree No.218/2013/ND-
CP dated 26 December 2013, detailing and guiding the implementation of the law on CIT.
For the Bank’s branch in Cambodia, MB shall calculate and determine its CIT in compliance 
with Cambodian regulations on corporate income tax. According to the Tax Act dated 8 
January 1997, the corporate income tax of the Bank’s branch in Cambodia is determined 
to be the greater of the minimum tax payable determined by 1% of total revenue (including 
value added tax) and 20% of profits earned. CIT of the Bank’s branch in Cambodia for the 
fiscal year ended 31 December 2022 is defined as 20% of profits earned.
For the Bank’s branch in Laos, MB shall calculate and determine its CIT in accordance with 
the income tax regulations in Laos. According to the Tax Ordinance No. 67 dated 18 June 
2019 issued by the Lao P.D.R Parliament and became effective from 17 February 2020, CIT 
of the branch is defined as 20% of the profit.
MB’s tax reports are subject to examination by the tax authorities. Because the application 
of tax laws and regulations to many types of transactions is susceptible to varying 
interpretations, amount reported in the consolidated financial statements could be 
changed later upon final determination of the tax authorities.
Current corporate income tax payables are determined based on taxable income of the 
period. Taxable income differs from the one reported in the consolidated statement of 
profit or loss since taxable income excludes incomes which are taxable or expenses which 
are deducted in prior periods due to the differences between MB’s accounting policies and 
the tax regulations. It also excludes tax exempted income and non-deductible expenses. 
The current corporate income tax payable of MB is calculated based on the statutory tax 
rates applicable at the end of the period.

TRANSACTIONS
45
During normal business operation, MB has undertaken transactions with other parties to 
which MB is related. A party is considered to be related if the party has ability to control or 
to influence other parties in making decision of financial policies and operational activities. 
A party is related to MB if: 
a. Directly, or indirectly through one or more intermediaries, the party: 
•	 Controls, is controlled by, or is under common control by MB (including parents and 
subsidiaries);
•	 Has an interest (owning 5% or more of the charter capital or voting share capital) in MB 
that gives it significant influence over MB; 
•	 Has joint control over MB;
b. The party is a joint venture in which MB is a venture or an associate (owning over 11% of 
the charter capital or voting share capital, but is not a subsidiary);
c. The party has a member which is the member of the key management personnel of MB 
or Board of Directors of MB; 
d. The party is a close member of the family of any individual referred to in (a) or (c); or
e. The party is an entity that is controlled, jointly controlled or significantly influenced by, or 
for which significant voting power in such company resides with, directly or indirectly, any 
individual referred to in (c) or (d).

FINANCIAL RISK 
MANAGEMENT POLICIES
This section provides information of MB’s exposure to risks and describes the policies used 
by the Management to control risks. The most important types of financial risks to which 
MB is exposed are credit risk, liquidity risk and market risk.
MB’s orientation is to become a diversified financial group. Therefore, the use of financial 
instruments, including funding from customers (including deposit and valuable papers 
issued) and investments in high quality financial assets has become key activities to help 
MB gain necessary interest rate gaps. From the risk management perspective, MB is 
required to maintain the structure of assets, liabilities and equity (including statement of 
financial position items and off-statement of financial position items) for the purpose of 
ensuring safety and mitigating risks in banking activities. In addition, MB has invested in 
securities or granted credit facilities to other banks. The risks related to currency exchange 
and interest rates have been managed through applying of position limits to restrict 
over-concentration and simultaneously participating in activities with balancing impact 
to minimise risks. By holding various assets being high quality financial instruments, the 
structure of MB’s consolidated statement of financial position would be able to protect MB 
from significant risks during its business processes and ensure liquidity. In addition, MB has 
been also involved in many derivatives transactions related to financial instruments such 
as currency forward commitments, currency swap commitments, and cross currency swap 
commitments for the purpose of managing interest rate risk and currency risk.
In the process of credit risk management, MB has adopted the Credit Handbook which 
provides in details the lending policies and procedures as well as implementation guidance 
on standardisation of MB’s credit activities. Liquidity risk is limited by holding appropriate 
amounts of cash and cash equivalents as demand deposits (“Nostro”), term deposits at the 
SBV and other credit institutions and valuable papers. The safety ratios with risk factors 
taken into account are also used to manage liquidity risk. MB has regularly assessed interest 
rate gaps, compared to the gaps of domestic markets and international markets to make 
timely adjustments. In addition, the application of internal risk management processes 
has become more efficient owing to the deployment of Centralised Capital Management 
System and Centralised Payment System in which all capital and payment transactions of 
MB are executed by the Head Office. Such centralisation has also helped MB to monitor 
capital movements more effectively and reduce any possible errors and unnecessarily 
complicated procedures

INTEREST RATE RISK
48
MB’s operations are subject to the risk of interest rate fluctuations to the extent that interest-
earning assets and interest-bearing liabilities mature at different times or in different 
amounts. Some assets have indefinite maturities or interest rate sensitivities and are not 
readily matched with specific liabilities.
The following table show MB’s assets and liabilities categorised by effective interest re-pricing 
period or maturity date and the effective interest rates as at the reporting date.
The effective interest rate re-pricing term is the remaining period from the reporting date to 
the latest interest rate re-pricing date of assets and liabilities items. The following assumptions 
and conditions are applied in the analysis of the effective interest rate re-pricing term of 
assets and liabilities of MB:
•	 Cash, gold, silver and gemstones; long-term investments and other assets (including 
fixed assets and some other assets) are classified as non-interest bearings;
•	 Deposits at the State Bank are classified as demand deposits, therefore effective interest 
re-pricing term is classified as up to one month;
•	 Held-for-trading debt securities are classified as up to one month;
•	 The effective interest rate re-pricing term of investment securities and trading securities 
is determined as follows:
	- Items with fixed interest for the duration of the contract: The effective interest rate re-
pricing term is based on the actual maturity date from the date of the consolidated 
financial statements;
	- Items with floating interest rates: The effective interest rate re-pricing term is based 
on the latest interest rate re-pricing date from the date of the consolidated financial 
statements;
	- Investment securities and trading securities which are equity securities are classified 
as non-interest bearings.
•	 The effective interest rate re-pricing term of deposits and loans to credit institutions, 
loans to customers granted and trusted for granting; due from the Government and 
the State Bank; deposits and loans from credit institutions; customers’ deposits; other 
borrowed and entrusted funds and valuable papers issued are determined as follows:
	- Items with fixed interest rates for the duration of the contract: The effective interest 
rate re-pricing term is based on the actual maturity date from the date of the 
consolidated statement of financial position;
	- Items with floating interest rate: The effective interest rate re-pricing term is based on 
the latest interest rate re-pricing date from the date of the consolidated statement 
of financial position;
•	 Other liabilities are classified as non-interest bearings due to interest re-pricing.

LIQUIDITY RISK 
50
Liquidity risk arises in MB’s funding activities in general and in the management of 
positions. It includes both the risk of being unable to fund assets at appropriate maturities 
and rates and the risk of being unable to liquidate an asset at a reasonable price and in 
an appropriate time frame.
MB adopts a risk measurement method that is appropriate to its operation scale and 
the availability of the information system, ensuring to meet the requirements for the risk 
mitigation.  It includes indicators related to cash flows, ability of capital mobilisation, and 
ability of asset liquidity of MB.  MB also has a designated unit focusing on obtaining 
update domestic and foreign economic information, which directly affects MB’s trading 
book and business strategies, as well as on forecasting movements of market factors such 
as the foreign exchange rate, interest rate and gold price for timely risk warnings. MB 
also establishes and applies a limit system and decision authority at each level based on

•	 Deposits and borrowings from credit institutions and customers’ deposits are 
determined based on the nature of these items or the maturity date on the contract.

and are therefore classified as demand deposits. The maturity period for borrowings 
and term deposits is determined based on the maturity date on the contract. In reality, 
these accounts may have been renewed and therefore have been maintained longer 
than the original maturity date; and
•	 The maturity period of fixed assets is determined as having term from (1) to (5) years.
